bullets.title: Professional Nursing Identity and Accountability
bullets.text: Professional identity is expressed through knowledge, conduct, communication and responsibility. Nurses are accountable for the decisions they make, the care they provide and the actions they delegate. Accountability also includes recognising limits and seeking help before patient safety is compromised.

bullets.title: Ethical Principles and Patient Rights
bullets.text: Ethical principles help nurses reason through choices that affect dignity, safety and fairness. They are not abstract ideas; they guide consent, truth-telling, advocacy, privacy and decisions about treatment.

bullets.title: Consent, Confidentiality and Documentation
bullets.text: Legal and professional duties protect patients from unwanted treatment, privacy breaches and unsafe continuity of care. Informed consent, confidentiality and accurate records are core nursing responsibilities.

bullets.title: Professional Communication, Delegation and Reflection
bullets.text: Professional nursing depends on clear communication, safe teamwork and willingness to reflect. Delegation can improve care, but the nurse remains responsible for assessing whether the task, person and circumstances are appropriate.
